title: Best tools to sync buying signals to LinkedIn ads
summary: Compare 9 tools that turn buying signals into LinkedIn ad audiences: contact vs account level, refresh speed, buying stages and other ad channels.
body_markdown:
The best tools for syncing buying signals to LinkedIn ad audiences build the audience from live signals, refresh it automatically as people move in and out of market, and target the specific people in the buying committee as well as the account. UserGems is the strongest fit for contact-level, signal-based audiences tied to buying stages and synced to LinkedIn plus Meta, Google, Bing and AdRoll. Demandbase and 6sense suit enterprise ABM suites, ZenABM and Metadata.io suit LinkedIn-heavy ad teams, Influ2 suits person-based ads, and HubSpot and LinkedIn's native Matched Audiences cover the basics.


## **Why sync buying signals to LinkedIn audiences at all?**


Most LinkedIn ABM programs start with a static list: upload 500 target accounts, layer on job titles, and run the same ads for a quarter. The problem is that most of those accounts aren't in-market at any given time, and the list ages the day you upload it.


Signal-based audiences fix the timing. When an account starts researching your category, a new VP joins, or a past champion lands at a target account, they enter the audience. When they go quiet or become an open opportunity, they drop out or move to a different ad track. Your spend follows the buyers who are actually moving.


## **Should LinkedIn audiences be account-level or contact-level?**


LinkedIn Matched Audiences supports both company lists and contact lists.


- **Account-level audiences** target everyone at a company who matches your job title and seniority filters. Reach is broad, and so is waste.
- **Contact-level audiences** target the named people in the buying committee: the new VP, the champion, the engaged evaluator. Smaller audiences, much tighter relevance, and you can align ads with what sales is sending those same people.


Most strong programs run both. Read more in[contact-level intent vs account-level intent](https://www.usergems.com/6sense-limitations/contact-level-intent-vs-account-level-intent-the-complete-guide) .


## **What to look for in a LinkedIn audience sync tool**


1. **Signal sources:** intent, website visits, job changes, new hires, product usage, CRM stage.
2. **Audience level:** company lists, contact lists, or both.
3. **Refresh:** does the audience update automatically, and how often?
4. **Buying stage logic:** can you run different ads by stage?
5. **Other channels:** Meta, Google, Bing and others from the same audience.
6. **Sales alignment:** do the same signals reach reps?


## **Best tools for LinkedIn buying signal audience sync at a glance**


1. **UserGems (Gem-E for ABM)**


- **Best for:** Signal-based buying committee audiences aligned with sales
- **Signal level:** Contact and account
- **Key strength:** Audiences built from live signals and Buying Stages; syncs to LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Bing, AdRoll
- **Watch out for:** Uses your ad accounts; it doesn't buy media itself
- **Pricing:** Credit-based packages; contact sales


1. **Demandbase**


- **Best for:** Enterprise ABM with buying group mapping
- **Signal level:** Account and people
- **Key strength:** Syncs account and people audiences to LinkedIn nightly
- **Watch out for:** Heavier platform to implement
- **Pricing:** Custom quote; no free plan or self-serve trial


1. **6sense**


- **Best for:** Enterprise ABM targeting by account buying stage
- **Signal level:** Mainly account
- **Key strength:** Dynamic segments as LinkedIn audiences; LinkedIn campaigns run from 6sense
- **Watch out for:** Stage logic is hard to explain to sales
- **Pricing:** Custom quote; no free plan or trial listed on G2


1. **Clay (Clay Ads)**


- **Best for:** GTM engineers building custom audiences
- **Signal level:** Mostly contact
- **Key strength:** Self-refreshing audiences synced to six ad platforms
- **Watch out for:** You design and maintain the audience logic
- **Pricing:** Free plan available; Clay Ads needs the Growth plan (listed at $446/mo, from $185/mo billed annually at the smallest tier)


1. **ZenABM**


- **Best for:** LinkedIn-first ABM teams that want engagement-based audiences
- **Signal level:** Account
- **Key strength:** Daily-refreshed company audiences from LinkedIn engagement and CRM
- **Watch out for:** Company-level audiences only on LinkedIn \[VERIFY\]
- **Pricing:** Public pricing: $59/mo (Starter) to $399/mo (Pro), two months free on annual


1. **Metadata.io**


- **Best for:** Demand gen teams automating paid campaigns
- **Signal level:** Account and contact (CSV, CRM)
- **Key strength:** Agents build audiences and run campaigns across 12 channels
- **Watch out for:** Full media automation, which is more than an audience sync
- **Pricing:** Custom quote; Capterra lists flat-rate plans from $5,650/mo


1. **Influ2**


- **Best for:** Person-based advertising to named contacts
- **Signal level:** Contact
- **Key strength:** Shows sales which contacts saw and clicked ads
- **Watch out for:** Bring your own signals to choose who to target \[VERIFY\]
- **Pricing:** Custom quote based on the number of people targeted, with ad fees bundled in


1. **HubSpot ads audiences**


- **Best for:** HubSpot users syncing CRM lists
- **Signal level:** Contact (company via lists)
- **Key strength:** Lists sync to LinkedIn and update as contacts move
- **Watch out for:** Only as smart as the signals in your HubSpot lists
- **Pricing:** LinkedIn ad campaigns on all HubSpot plans; ad automations need Marketing Hub Starter or above


1. **LinkedIn Matched Audiences (native)**


- **Best for:** Simple, low-cost list targeting
- **Signal level:** Contact and account
- **Key strength:** Built into Campaign Manager
- **Watch out for:** Manual uploads go stale without a sync tool
- **Pricing:** Included with LinkedIn Ads


## **The 9 best tools for syncing buying signals to LinkedIn audiences**


### [1. UserGems](https://www.usergems.com/) **(Gem-E for ABM)**


UserGems is the AI command center for outbound and ABM. UserGems keeps every account and person that matters to you up to date, with their buying signals, relationship with you, score and buying stage.


Gem-E for ABM turns that graph into always-on ad audiences. You build Audiences from signals (past champions, new hires and promotions, buying group activity, contact and account intent, website visits, product and engagement signals) and from Buying Stages, then sync them to LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Bing and AdRoll, plus your MAP. Because audiences are contact-level, you can target the specific people in the buying committee, run different creative by stage, and drop accounts out when they become open opportunities.


The same signals reach sales: reps see them in the AI Chrome Extension and Slack, and the Gem-E Writing Agent drafts outreach to the same people. Customers have cut their ABM process from about four weeks to about two with Gem-E, and run 3X the volume of ABM accounts while keeping 10%+ conversion to demo requests.


**Best for:** teams that want ads and outbound hitting the same in-market people. **Watch out for:** UserGems builds and syncs the audiences; your ad platforms still serve the ads and hold the budget. Audiences sync automatically on weekdays and you can choose the sync frequency. The first LinkedIn sync takes about 24 to 48 hours, and LinkedIn won't serve until at least 300 people match.


### [2. Demandbase](https://www.demandbase.com/)


Demandbase syncs both account and people audiences to LinkedIn Campaign Manager, where they appear as a third-party source. The first sync can take one to two days, and later syncs run nightly ([Demandbase support](https://support.demandbase.com/hc/en-us/articles/4405716770843) ). Its buying group AI maps contacts to roles.


**Best for:** enterprise ABM teams already on Demandbase. **Watch out for:** implementation and admin effort for smaller teams.


### [3. 6sense](https://6sense.com/)


6sense lets marketers use its dynamic segments as LinkedIn audiences, target accounts by buying stage, and run LinkedIn campaigns from inside 6sense ([Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231115278482/en/6sense-Launches-LinkedIn-Campaign-Management-Integration) ).


**Best for:** 6sense customers targeting by account buying stage. **Watch out for:** segments are driven mainly by account-level intent, and the score behind each stage is hard to see.


### [4. Clay (Clay Ads)](https://www.clay.com/ads)


Clay Ads builds audiences from CRM, warehouse, intent and 200+ data providers, and syncs them to LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Bing, Reddit and Vibe.co as self-refreshing audiences with suppression lists.


**Best for:** teams with a GTM engineer. **Watch out for:** scoring, stages and audience rules are yours to build and maintain.


### [5. ZenABM](https://zenabm.com/)


ZenABM is built for ABM on LinkedIn. It pulls company-level engagement from the LinkedIn API, scores accounts and assigns stages, then syncs dynamic, daily-refreshed company audiences to LinkedIn. It also pushes engagement data into HubSpot and Salesforce, and lists its pricing publicly.


**Best for:** LinkedIn-first teams that want engagement-based retargeting and reporting. **Watch out for:** its strongest signal is engagement with your own ads, so in-market accounts that haven't seen your ads need another signal source.


### [6. Metadata.io](https://metadata.io/)


Metadata.io uses AI agents to plan, build audiences and run campaigns across LinkedIn, Meta, Google and other channels. Audiences can use firmographics, Bombora and G2 intent, CRM stage and CSV uploads.


**Best for:** demand gen teams that want campaign execution automated. **Watch out for:** it's a full media automation platform, a bigger decision than adding an audience sync.


### [7. Influ2](https://www.influ2.com/)


Influ2 runs person-based ads to named contacts synced from your CRM across LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, Google and more, and shows sales which contacts saw or clicked each ad.


**Best for:** teams that already know exactly which people to target. **Watch out for:** you still need a source of signals to decide who goes in the list.


### [8. HubSpot ads audiences](https://www.hubspot.com/products/marketing/ads)


HubSpot's LinkedIn Ads integration syncs contact lists to LinkedIn and adds or removes contacts as they move through your funnel.


**Best for:** HubSpot customers who want CRM-based audiences fast. **Watch out for:** audiences only reflect the signals already in HubSpot properties and lists.


### **9. LinkedIn Matched Audiences (native)**


LinkedIn's built-in Matched Audiences let you upload company and contact lists, and retarget website visitors in Campaign Manager.


**Best for:** getting started. **Watch out for:** manual CSV uploads don't refresh, so in-market accounts enter late and out-of-market ones stay in.


## **How do you run LinkedIn ads by buying stage?**


- **Awareness and Interest:** point-of-view content and thought leadership to the buying committee.
- **Consideration:** customer stories, comparison content and product proof.
- **Decision:** demo offers and ROI proof, timed with sales outreach to the same people.
- **Open opportunity:** move contacts into a deal-support track or suppress them.


For the full motion, read[the signal-based ABM guide](https://www.usergems.com/guides/the-signal-based-abm-guide) or compare more[contact-based marketing tools](https://www.usergems.com/blog/contact-based-marketing-tools) .


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **Can I sync intent data to LinkedIn automatically?**


Yes. Tools like UserGems, Demandbase, 6sense, Clay and ZenABM sync signal-based audiences to LinkedIn Campaign Manager on a schedule, so accounts and people enter and exit as signals change.


### **Is it better to target accounts or contacts on LinkedIn?**


Run both. Account targeting gives reach across the company; contact targeting focuses spend on the named people in the buying committee who are showing buying behavior.


### **What buying signals work best for LinkedIn ad audiences?**


Contact-level signals like new hires and promotions in your persona, past champions at new accounts and known website visitors, combined with account-level intent and buying stage.


### **Does LinkedIn have a minimum audience size?**


Yes. A LinkedIn audience needs at least 300 matched members before a campaign starts delivering. Contact list uploads need at least 300 contacts (LinkedIn recommends 10,000 or more), and up to 300,000 per list. Not every contact matches a LinkedIn profile, so start with a bigger list than the 300 you need.


### **Can the same audience run on Meta and Google?**


With most sync tools, yes. UserGems syncs the same signal-based audiences to LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Bing and AdRoll.
